work.title: Homily on the Annunciation I (25 March)

paragraphs.text: to the priests. And I will have to suffer because of my marriage and my own choice, and he will cut off your head with an axe. Moreover, you speak to me here on earth, before the doors of my room, yet you promise to bring me a bridegroom from heaven. What heavenly being desires marriage? All heavenly beings are spirits without bodies. And the angel answered: “For the sake of those with bodies and those without bodies, he will be called the Son of the Most High.” The virgin said, “Where, then, will he have a father, the one who, as you say, is to be born from me?” And the angel answered, “This is the wonder for you: you do not know a man, yet you will give birth to the one of whom I speak, and the child will not be fatherless. He will come out of your womb without damaging its doors, and you will not lose your virginity. You will nurse the one who is born, and you will acknowledge as God the one born from you. You will carry the infant in your arms, and you will see him upon the cherubim. For to this one born from you, O virgin, the Lord God will give the throne of his father David, and his kingdom will have no end.” The virgin answered, “Without meaning to, you too have gone astray in speaking. Your own mouth has accused you. Your own lips have become evidence against you. Just now you said,

‘The one who is born will be called the Son of the Most High,’ but now you say, ‘the son of David.’ What does this mean? Whenever you wish, you lift my mind up to heaven, and whenever you wish, you bring it down to earth. Which statement am I to believe, the first or the second? For you say that the Lord God will give him the throne of his father David, and his kingdom will have no end. None of the kings was free from death. No one escaped the end common to all. The immortal Master takes them all away. Worms devour them all. None of the kings escaped the gates of Hades. No one leaped over its snares; no one escaped its nets. Neither Saul, the first to establish the royal crown, nor David, who through the horn was revealed and declared worthy of kingship, nor Samuel, the father of kings, who through olive oil recognized the unworthy, nor Solomon the wise, who exposed a slanderous lie with a sword, nor Hezekiah, who through tears reversed the decree of death. How, then, will my son reign forever?” And the angel answered, “This, Mary, is the wonder and the mystery for you. For everyone has died, but your son will conquer death. He will raise the dead, open the tombs, and shatter the keys of Hades.

He will raise many bodies of those who have died. For, being born of the immortal one, he will put death to death. Do not disbelieve, lest you fall into guilt. For he of whom I speak has already leaped into your womb through your hearing, renewing your womb. And the virgin said, “So that I may believe you about him, first explain to me how he is both the Son of the Most High and the son of David— he who, as you say, is to be born of me on earth, and whom you claim will be without a father. How, then, have you named two fathers?” And the angel said, “First learn, and then dispute. When I say ‘Son of the Most High,’ I indicate the Father who begot him before the ages, without passion. When I say ‘son of David,’ I say this because you descend from your forefather David. Accept the word of my message with certainty and keep it. For I too am a servant of him whom you are to see working within you as God.” And the angel sent to her, having spoken in this way, left her. And Mary pondered within herself: “Shall I tell Joseph this? Or shall I rather conceal this secret? What if the one who came has lied? Why should I provoke the old man’s tongue to anger?” And while she was uncertain about this, her womb was swelling, and the child was moving within. Mary did not know what to do. She piled many garments over her womb,

wanting to spare Joseph. But she could not hide a city standing on a hilltop. The sight of her womb struck Joseph, and, looking up from below, he examined the virgin’s womb. He wanted to question her, but he was compelled to remain silent. And he wanted to conceal her, as one who had sold the vessel of her virginity [?]. Yet her former way of life held him back, so that now he tormented his soul with sorrow. “Oh, woe is me!” he said. “What shall I do? Her face is a virgin’s, her walk is a virgin’s, her eyes are a virgin’s, her smile is a virgin’s, her speech is a virgin’s, but her womb is not a virgin’s, but a mother’s. I cannot bear it. Shall I reveal the matter? But if I expose Mary, the shame will be shared. Shall I raise my voice and cry out? For I am afraid that I might become the accuser of a child conceived without seed. No one is the child’s accuser, since the one being born has no one who sowed him. In every way, both speaking and remaining silent bring me trouble. What, then, shall I do? Shall I call her and question her? Or shall I expose her before questioning her?” But Scripture bears witness, saying, “Reprove, but do not act.” Calling her with an angry face, he judged the one who was in her womb. The judge sat and said, “Tell me, Mary, what has happened? Do not hide from me what has befallen you. There is no one here listening to this conversation. I know how to keep

a secret. No one shall hear of this. Tell me alone: where has this come from? Show me this child's father, so that I may forgive your sin. For you will deserve mercy, as a woman overcome by her thoughts.” Then the pure virgin Mary said, weeping, “If you are looking for this child's father, you will find him nowhere. And if you think him an orphan, that does not apply to him either.” Joseph said, “Mary, you cannot even lie! For how can he neither be an orphan nor have a father?” Mary said, “If I tell you the truth, you will not believe me. You look at my womb, but you do not see the one hidden within it. You examine my belly, but you do not consider that the one born of the Father, from the womb before the morning star, is dwelling there. If I tell you what the angel said, you will say, ‘You are making yourself your own witness. Your testimony is not true. Bring someone who heard, or someone who stood there. Bring trustworthy witnesses.’ If you seek this, you will never find it. For one was sent by one to one woman, and for the sake of the one to be born, he spoke to her alone. There was no one else. If anyone had been there, he would surely have wanted to be the father of the child to be born.” And when he did not believe the virgin, realizing this,

the woman Mary turned to another thought and said, even against her will, “Since I am so utterly mistrusted, and truly my womb betrays me, and the child exposes me as he leaps within my womb, why do I myself anger Joseph still more? Let me shut off my reply with silence; let me bind my lips with silence and plead unseen with the angel. Where are you now, you who said to me, ‘Rejoice’? Tell me where you dwell, so that I may go there and cling to your neck until you come and make it clear to Joseph whose Son this is who plays upon the bed of my womb. I cannot bear to see the old man lamenting under this burden, and I do not know where you are delaying. Come and plead my case.” While Mary was saying these things, the angel quickly came to Joseph and, making the matter clear, stopped him from driving out the virgin. “Do not be afraid, Joseph, to take your wife, who is not joined to you in marriage, but appointed to serve God's mysteries. I call her your wife, but you are not the father.” Do not seek a father on earth or a mother in heaven. For his nature is entirely free from orphanhood. For he alone was born of the one, once before the ages, and again, he alone of her alone, is born as he alone knows. Do not trouble Mary. Do not make what comes from Mary a cause of grief. Do not ask how, lest you be harmed by

the light. Do not disturb the ark, lest you [?] what is in it. A vessel without blemish, a dwelling without defilement, a glass vessel undisturbed, a birth without seed, a virgin without marriage, a pure woman without a bridal chamber, a stone not cut out, a locked city, a sealed spring, an unsown field, an unplanted vine, an indescribable wonder, an incomprehensible birth. But if you do not believe what I am telling you, wait for the time of the birth. Then, if Mary groans or cries out like other women, he is a man and not God in the flesh, who is being born of Mary. And Joseph answered, “If what you say is so, O angel, why did the nations rage, and the peoples meditate on vain things?” And the angel said, “If you wish to learn, learn quickly. For the Lord said to the one being born, ‘You are my Son; today I have begotten you.’ For to him belong glory and power, honor and worship, now and always and forever and ever. Amen.
